title: Post-assassination letters telling Ruth Paine to keep quiet about Oswald

tellings.quote: >> And Arthur Young's wife is telling Ruth, her daughter-in-law, ix nay on the Oswald gay, right?

plain: After President John F. Kennedy was killed in 1963, Ruth Paine, a woman connected to the accused assassin Lee Harvey Oswald, was told in letters to keep quiet about him, according to the researcher Peter Levenda. He says the letters came from her mother-in-law, Ruth Forbes Paine Young, the wife of Arthur Young, and sums up their message as "ix nay on the Oswald gay", pig Latin for "don't talk about Oswald". Levenda cites the letters between the two women, which went between Pennsylvania and Texas in 1963 and 1964, and if he is right, Paine's own family was trying to control what she said about Oswald.
